note: Correct answer is listed first; choices are shuffled when a game is built.

questions.text: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.quip: Hot take: it's the Sun. Literally.

questions.text: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.quip: Mars: rusty, dusty, and totally red-y.

questions.text: What is the biggest planet in our solar system?
questions.quip: You could fit over 1,000 Earths inside Jupiter. Big house!

questions.text: How many planets are in our solar system?
questions.quip: Eight! Sorry, Pluto — you're still a star to us.

questions.text: What do astronauts wear to breathe in space?
questions.quip: Pajamas are comfy, but terrible at making oxygen.

questions.text: Which planet has the most famous rings?
questions.quip: Saturn put a ring on it. Lots of rings, actually.

questions.text: What is the Moon mostly covered with?
questions.quip: Sorry, cheese fans. Rock and dust only.

questions.text: What pulls things down toward the ground?
questions.quip: Gravity: keeping your snacks on the table since forever.

questions.text: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.quip: Mercury is so close to the Sun it needs serious sunscreen.

questions.text: What do we call a group of stars that makes a picture in the sky?
questions.quip: Connect-the-dots, cosmic edition!

questions.text: Which planet spins on its side, like a rolling ball?
questions.quip: Uranus: the solar system's professional roller.

questions.text: What is the name of the galaxy we live in?
questions.quip: Home sweet spiral.

questions.text: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.quip: One small step for a player, one giant leap for your score.

questions.text: Which planet has the shortest year?
questions.quip: Mercury has a birthday every 88 days. Huge cake budget.

questions.text: What is the hottest planet in our solar system?
questions.quip: Venus: thick clouds, trapped heat, zero chill.

questions.text: Why does the Moon seem to change shape during the month?
choices: We see different parts of its lit side
questions.quip: Earth's shadow only shows up during eclipses!

questions.text: About how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.quip: Your sunshine is about 8 minutes old. Still fresh!

questions.text: What is the largest volcano in the solar system?
questions.quip: Olympus Mons, on Mars, is about 2.5 times taller than Everest.

questions.text: Which planet has the Great Red Spot, a giant storm?
questions.quip: A storm bigger than Earth, raging for centuries. Bring an umbrella.

questions.text: What do we call a space rock that burns up in Earth's sky?
questions.quip: Quick, make a wish — it's a meteor!

questions.text: What is the largest moon in our solar system?
questions.quip: Ganymede is even bigger than the planet Mercury.

questions.text: Which spacecraft was the first to leave the heliosphere?
questions.quip: Launched in 1977 and still sending postcards.

questions.text: What is the name of Saturn's largest moon?
questions.quip: Titan has lakes — of liquid methane. Not great for swimming.

questions.text: About how many Earth days does Mars take to orbit the Sun?
questions.quip: A Mars year is almost two Earth years. Double summer break?

questions.text: What is the closest star system to our Sun?
questions.quip: Only about 4.4 light-years away. Practically neighbors!

questions.text: Io, the most volcanic place known, is a moon of which planet?
questions.quip: Io has hundreds of active volcanoes. Talk about a hot spot.

questions.text: What will our Sun become near the end of its life?
questions.quip: Red giant first, then a white dwarf. Billions of years away — relax.

questions.text: What is the edge of a black hole, past which nothing escapes?
questions.quip: Past the event horizon, even light can't get out.

questions.text: Which dwarf planet is the largest object in the asteroid belt?
questions.quip: Ceres: the asteroid belt's heavyweight champion.

questions.text: Which space telescope, launched in 2021, sees mainly in infrared?
questions.quip: It parked about 1.5 million km away to keep its cool.

questions.text: What is the largest animal on Earth?
questions.quip: Longer than a school bus and heavier than a herd of elephants.

questions.text: Which animal can change the color of its skin?
questions.quip: Now you see it, now you… still kind of see it.

questions.text: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.quip: Eight legs and zero shoelaces to tie.

questions.text: What sweet food do bees make?
questions.quip: Bees: tiny, buzzy, and very sweet.

questions.text: Which animal is the tallest in the world?
questions.quip: Great view up there, long way to swallow.

questions.text: What is a baby kangaroo called?
questions.quip: A joey rides in mom's pouch. Best seat in the house.

questions.text: Which bird can turn its head almost all the way around?
questions.quip: Owls can turn their heads about 270 degrees. Don't try it at home!

questions.text: What is the fastest land animal?
questions.quip: Zero to highway speed in about three seconds.

questions.text: Which African animal looks like a horse with black and white stripes?
questions.quip: Every zebra's stripes are unique, like a fingerprint.

questions.text: What do caterpillars turn into?
questions.quip: From very hungry to very fancy.

questions.text: Which mammal can truly fly?
questions.quip: Flying squirrels glide. Bats actually fly!

questions.text: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.quip: Three hearts and blue blood. Very royal.

questions.text: What is a group of lions called?
questions.quip: A pride of lions — and they know it.

questions.text: Which is the largest big cat?
questions.quip: The biggest kitty on the planet. Do not pet.

questions.text: What do giant pandas mostly eat?
questions.quip: Pandas munch bamboo for up to 14 hours a day.

questions.text: Which of these animals is NOT a mammal?
questions.quip: Sharks are fish; dolphins and whales are mammals.

questions.text: How do frogs take in most of the water they need?
questions.quip: No cups needed — frogs soak it up through their skin.

questions.text: What is a baby goat called?
questions.quip: Kids are kids. Literally.

questions.text: Which bird lays the largest eggs?
questions.quip: One ostrich egg makes an omelet for the whole family.

questions.text: Which animal finds food in the dark using echoes?
questions.quip: Bats shout and listen for echoes. Nature's sonar!

questions.text: Which mammal lays eggs and has a duck-like bill?
questions.quip: The platypus: nature's mix-and-match project.

questions.text: How many compartments does a cow's stomach have?
questions.quip: Four compartments, one very long lunch.

questions.text: Which animal has fingerprints almost identical to humans?
questions.quip: Koala fingerprints could fool a detective. Suspicious!

questions.text: What is the fastest bird when diving?
questions.quip: Over 300 km/h in a dive. Speed limit? Never heard of it.

questions.text: What is a group of crows called?
questions.quip: Spooky name, very clever birds.

questions.text: Which animal has the largest eyes in the animal kingdom?
questions.quip: Eyes the size of dinner plates. Great for spotting snacks.

questions.text: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can…
questions.quip: Reverse gear: unlocked.

questions.text: Which animal can sleep up to 20 hours a day?
questions.quip: Koalas: undefeated champions of the nap.

questions.text: What is a baby swan called?
questions.quip: Cygnet: a fancy name for a fluffy grey baby.

questions.text: Which amphibian can regrow legs and even parts of its heart?
questions.quip: Axolotls: the regrowing superheroes of the pond.

questions.text: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.quip: The Pacific is bigger than all the land on Earth put together.

questions.text: Why does ocean water taste salty?
questions.quip: Great for waves, terrible for lemonade.

questions.text: Which ocean animal has eight arms?
questions.quip: Eight arms: excellent at group hugs.

questions.text: What do we call a giant ocean wave caused by an earthquake?
questions.quip: Scientists watch the oceans so people get warnings in time.

questions.text: Which sea animal is a mammal that breathes air?
questions.quip: Dolphins pop up for air — and for applause.

questions.text: Which fish lives safely among the stinging arms of sea anemones?
questions.quip: A slimy coat protects them. Gross, but genius.

questions.text: What covers most of Earth's surface?
questions.quip: About 71% water. Maybe we should call it Planet Ocean!

questions.text: Which crab moves into bigger empty shells as it grows?
questions.quip: Moving day, every time it grows!

questions.text: What colorful underwater structure is built by tiny animals?
questions.quip: Coral reefs are built by tiny animals called polyps.

questions.text: Which ocean reptile lays its eggs on sandy beaches?
questions.quip: Baby sea turtles race to the waves right after hatching.

questions.text: What is the deepest known point in the ocean?
questions.quip: Almost 11 km deep. Everest would fit with room to spare.

questions.text: What is the largest fish in the ocean?
questions.quip: Huge fish, tiny menu: it eats plankton.

questions.text: What mostly causes ocean tides?
questions.quip: The Moon pulls, the ocean follows. The Sun helps a little too.

questions.text: Which is the smallest of Earth's oceans?
questions.quip: Smallest, iciest, coolest — literally.

questions.text: How do fish breathe underwater?
questions.quip: Gills pull oxygen straight out of the water.

questions.text: What is a group of fish swimming together called?
questions.quip: A school of fish. No homework, though.

questions.text: Which sea creature squirts ink to escape danger?
questions.quip: Squirt, swirl, and — poof — gone.

questions.text: Which sea creature has no brain, no heart and no bones?
questions.quip: And it has been drifting along for over 500 million years.

questions.text: In seahorses, which parent carries the eggs until they hatch?
questions.quip: Seahorse dads: pregnancy pros.

questions.text: What is the world's largest coral reef system?
questions.quip: It's so big it can be seen from space.

questions.text: Which ocean zone, starting around 1,000 m deep, gets no sunlight?
questions.quip: So dark that many animals make their own light.

questions.text: What do we call living things that make their own light?
questions.quip: Glow-in-the-dark, no batteries required.

questions.text: Which current carries warm water from the Gulf of Mexico toward Europe?
questions.quip: It helps keep parts of Europe milder than you'd expect.

questions.text: About how much of Earth's water is in the oceans?
questions.quip: Only about 3% is fresh water. Save some for the plants!

questions.text: What is the long underwater mountain range in the middle of the Atlantic?
questions.quip: Earth's longest mountain range is mostly underwater.

questions.text: Which fish can walk on land using its fins?
questions.quip: Mudskippers: part fish, part hiking enthusiast.

questions.text: Which gas do ocean algae release that we breathe?
questions.quip: Tiny ocean algae make a huge share of the air we breathe.

questions.text: What is the name of the ocean that surrounds Antarctica?
questions.quip: The fifth official ocean — and a chilly one.

questions.text: Which shark is the largest predatory fish?
questions.quip: Big, toothy, and mostly misunderstood.

questions.text: How long can a sperm whale hold its breath?
questions.quip: Ninety minutes on one breath. Please don't try it in the bathtub.

questions.text: What does the word "dinosaur" mean?
questions.quip: Terrible lizard — though many were peaceful plant-eaters.

questions.text: Which dinosaur had three horns on its face?
questions.quip: Three horns: one for each bad hair day.

questions.text: Which dinosaur had big plates along its back?
questions.quip: Stegosaurus: a walking, spiky fence.

questions.text: Tyrannosaurus rex had very short…
questions.quip: Huge teeth, tiny arms. High-fives were tricky.

questions.text: Which dinosaur's name means "tyrant lizard king"?
questions.quip: A royal title for a royally big chomper.

questions.text: How do we know about dinosaurs today?
questions.quip: Fossils are nature's time capsules.

questions.text: Which long-necked dinosaur could reach the tops of trees?
questions.quip: Brachiosaurus never needed a ladder.

questions.text: Did dinosaurs and people live at the same time?
questions.quip: Dinosaurs were gone about 66 million years before the first people.

questions.text: Which flying reptile lived at the time of the dinosaurs?
questions.quip: Not technically a dinosaur — but a great flyer!

questions.text: Baby dinosaurs hatched from…
questions.quip: Some dinosaur eggs were as big as a melon.

questions.text: About when did most dinosaurs die out?
questions.quip: A giant space rock had a very bad day — and so did the dinosaurs.

questions.text: What is a scientist who studies fossils called?
questions.quip: Archaeologists dig up human history. Paleontologists dig up dinosaurs.

questions.text: Which animals alive today are descended from dinosaurs?
questions.quip: Next time you see a pigeon, say hi to a tiny dinosaur.

questions.text: Which dinosaur had a bony club at the end of its tail?
questions.quip: Built like a tank, swings like a batter.

questions.text: About how big was a real Velociraptor?
questions.quip: Movies made them huge. Real ones were turkey-sized — with feathers!

questions.text: Which dinosaur had a big sail on its back and probably ate fish?
questions.quip: Spinosaurus: part dinosaur, part sailboat.

questions.text: In which period did Tyrannosaurus rex live?
questions.quip: T. rex lived near the very end of the dinosaur age.

questions.text: What are dinosaur footprints preserved in rock called?
questions.quip: Footprints even tell us how fast dinosaurs walked.

questions.text: Which group of giant long-necked dinosaurs were the biggest land animals ever?
questions.quip: Long neck, long tail, very long lunch.

questions.text: What did Triceratops probably use its horns for?
questions.quip: Part shield, part showing off.

questions.text: Which dinosaur was the first to be scientifically named, in 1824?
questions.quip: Named before anyone had even invented the word "dinosaur."

questions.text: What is the event that wiped out the dinosaurs called?
questions.quip: An asteroid about 10 km wide ended a 165-million-year run.

questions.text: In which country is the crater from the dinosaur-ending asteroid?
questions.quip: The Chicxulub crater is buried under the Yucatán Peninsula.

questions.text: Which period of the dinosaur age came first?
questions.quip: Triassic, Jurassic, Cretaceous — the original dinosaur trilogy.

questions.text: What was unusual about the small dinosaur Microraptor?
questions.quip: Four feathered wings! Nature tried a biplane.

questions.text: What is the name of a famous, nearly complete T. rex skeleton?
questions.quip: Sue is about 90% complete. Not bad for 67 million years old.

questions.text: Pachycephalosaurus is named for its unusually thick…
questions.quip: Thick-headed lizard. It's a compliment, honestly.

questions.text: Roughly how long did non-bird dinosaurs live on Earth?
questions.quip: Humans have been around for a tiny fraction of that.

questions.text: Which supercontinent existed when the first dinosaurs appeared?
questions.quip: All the continents were one big block. Road trip!

questions.text: What is a coprolite?
questions.quip: Yes, scientists study fossil poop. Science is glamorous!

questions.text: Which fruit is yellow and curved?
questions.quip: Bananas: the original snack with built-in wrapping.

questions.text: Which crunchy orange vegetable do rabbits love?
questions.quip: Crunchy, orange, and great for your eyes.

questions.text: What is the main ingredient in guacamole?
questions.quip: Holy guacamole, you got it!

questions.text: Which drink do we get from cows?
questions.quip: Moo-velous answer!

questions.text: Pizza first comes from which country?
questions.quip: Mamma mia, that's right!

questions.text: What do you get when you heat corn kernels until they burst?
questions.quip: Pop, pop, hooray!

questions.text: Which fruit keeps the doctor away, in a famous saying?
questions.quip: An apple a day… and a quiz every night.

questions.text: What color is the inside of a watermelon, usually?
questions.quip: It's over 90% water — the name says it all.

questions.text: Which food do we get from chickens?
questions.quip: Which came first? Doesn't matter — you got it.

questions.text: What is the frozen dessert made from milk or cream and sugar?
questions.quip: Brain freeze: totally worth it.

questions.text: Which spice is the most expensive by weight?
questions.quip: Saffron threads are picked from flowers by hand.

questions.text: Sushi comes from which country?
questions.quip: Rice, fish, and a lot of skill.

questions.text: What is tofu made from?
questions.quip: Soy milk, curdled and pressed. Tasty science!

questions.text: Which nut is used to make marzipan?
questions.quip: Almonds plus sugar equals tiny edible sculptures.

questions.text: What makes bread dough rise and get fluffy?
questions.quip: Tiny yeast make bubbles. Bread says thank you.

questions.text: Which fruit has its seeds on the outside?
questions.quip: About 200 seeds per strawberry. Count them later.

questions.text: What is the main ingredient in hummus?
questions.quip: Chickpeas, blended into something wonderful.

questions.text: Which vegetable can make you cry when you cut it?
questions.quip: Onions: emotional damage, delicious results.

questions.text: Paella is a famous rice dish from which country?
questions.quip: Cooked in a wide pan, shared with everyone.

questions.text: Which of these is a fruit, scientifically speaking?
questions.quip: Tomato: a fruit by science, a vegetable by salad.

questions.text: What is the main green herb in classic pesto?
questions.quip: Basil, garlic, pine nuts, cheese and oil. Green magic.

questions.text: Which rice is traditionally used to make risotto?
questions.quip: Arborio releases starch for that creamy texture.

questions.text: Lack of vitamin C causes which disease?
questions.quip: Old-time sailors learned this one the hard way.

questions.text: Which food can last thousands of years and still be edible?
questions.quip: Archaeologists have found ancient honey that was still good!

questions.text: Kimchi is a fermented dish from which country?
questions.quip: Spicy, tangy, and full of good bacteria.

questions.text: Chocolate is made from the beans of which plant?
questions.quip: People in Mesoamerica drank chocolate thousands of years ago.

questions.text: What does the Scoville scale measure?
questions.quip: From a bell pepper's zero to "call the fire brigade."

questions.text: Which country produces the most coffee in the world?
questions.quip: Brazil has been the top coffee grower for over 150 years.

questions.text: Which vegetable is used to make sauerkraut?
questions.quip: Fermented cabbage: crunchy, tangy, and very German.

questions.text: Quinoa was first grown in which mountain region?
questions.quip: The Incas called it the "mother of all grains."
